The quality or skill of giving an engaging or compelling performance; a stage presence.
s.x: The act was clean and well-rehearsed, but the performers lacked the showmanship that would have made it great.

s.g: Something that exhibits exceptional quality, something worth being shown.
Something made specifically to be displayed.
A building or estate shown for its beauty or noteworthiness.
A location kept for display only.
A video portfolio demonstrating the talents of an actor, director, etc.
A room in a business set aside for the display of the company's products.
(dated) A room or apartment where a show is exhibited.
To inspect merchandise in a physical store, then purchase the identical product from an online merchant; to use a physical store as a showroom for an online merchant.
s.x: This new phone looks good, but I want to go to the mall and showroom it before buying.

s.g: The act or practice of inspecting the merchandise in a physical store, then purchasing the identical product from an online merchant.
The act or practice of using a physical store as a showroom for an online merchant.
s.x: Traditional retailers are devising strategies to counteract the threat from showrooming.

showrooming.f: present participle and gerund of showroom

s.g: (television) The person in overall charge of the production of a television series.

shows.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of show

s.g: A performance or segment of a theatrical production that induces a positive audience reaction strong enough to pause the production.
Any impediment that prevents all further progress.
(computing) A software bug that must be fixed before any further development is possible.
Characteristic of a showstopper; breathtaking.
(software engineering, of bugs) Critical; major.
The time at which an entertainment event is set to begin.
(figurative) The time for action.
A declaration that something is about to happen, particularly that the person speaking is about to act.
(sometimes derogatory) Calling attention; flashy; standing out to the eye.
Making a striking or aesthetically pleasing display.
s.x: showy flowers

s.g: (informal, chiefly of a literary work) Inclined to showing (by conveying an impression so that events are described in the narrative), instead of telling (by explicitly stating facts).
(automotive) Synonym of shock absorber.
